text: Be not too tame neither; but let your own discretion be your tutor.
plain: Rules only get you part of the way. Trust your own judgment for the rest.

text:
No, let the candied tongue lick absurd pomp,
And crook the pregnant hinges of the knee
Where thrift may follow fawning.
plain: Let others grovel for advantage. A real friend doesn't flatter you for a cut.

text:
And blessed are those
Whose blood and judgement are so well co-mingled
That they are not a pipe for Fortune’s finger
To sound what stop she please. Give me that man
That is not passion’s slave, and I will wear him
In my heart’s core, ay, in my heart of heart,
As I do thee.
plain: Be the person luck and mood can't play like an instrument. That's who earns real love.

text:
But what we do determine, oft we break.
Purpose is but the slave to memory,
Of violent birth, but poor validity:
Which now, like fruit unripe, sticks on the tree,
But fall unshaken when they mellow be.
plain: Resolutions are strong when made and weak a week later. Build the habit, not the mood.

text:
Most necessary ’tis that we forget
To pay ourselves what to ourselves is debt.
What to ourselves in passion we propose,
The passion ending, doth the purpose lose.
plain: We forget the promises we make ourselves. When the feeling fades, the plan goes with it.

text:
The great man down, you mark his favourite flies,
The poor advanc’d makes friends of enemies;
And hitherto doth love on fortune tend:
For who not needs shall never lack a friend,
And who in want a hollow friend doth try,
Directly seasons him his enemy.
plain: People stick around while you're winning and vanish when you fall. Test friends in hard times.

text:
Our wills and fates do so contrary run
That our devices still are overthrown.
Our thoughts are ours, their ends none of our own.
plain: You control your plans, not how they end. Make them anyway.

text: The lady protests too much, methinks.
plain: When someone defends too hard, something is off.

text: Why, let the strucken deer go weep, The hart ungalled play; For some must watch, while some must sleep, So runs the world away.
plain: Some people suffer while others play. That's how the world runs, so don't take it personally.

text: Call me what instrument you will, though you can fret me, you cannot play upon me.
plain: You can irritate me but you can't work me like a tool.

text:
My words fly up, my thoughts remain below.
Words without thoughts never to heaven go.
plain: Saying the right thing without meaning it gets you nowhere.

text: Assume a virtue, if you have it not.
plain: Act like the person you want to be before you are. The habit builds the person.

text:
Refrain tonight,
And that shall lend a kind of easiness
To the next abstinence. The next more easy;
For use almost can change the stamp of nature,
And either curb the devil, or throw him out
With wondrous potency.
plain: Say no tonight. Tomorrow's no is easier, and habit can rewrite your nature.

text:
I must be cruel, only to be kind:
Thus bad begins, and worse remains behind.
plain: Sometimes a hard thing now is the kind thing, and the worst is still ahead.

text: Your worm is your only emperor for diet. We fat all creatures else to fat us, and we fat ourselves for maggots. Your fat king and your lean beggar is but variable service,—two dishes, but to one table. That’s the end.
plain: King and beggar both end up as worm food. Status doesn't survive death.

text:
Two thousand souls and twenty thousand ducats
Will not debate the question of this straw!
This is th’imposthume of much wealth and peace,
That inward breaks, and shows no cause without
Why the man dies.
plain: Armies fight over a patch of dirt that's worth nothing. Comfort breeds pointless quarrels.

text: Lord, we know what we are, but know not what we may be.
plain: You know who you are today. You have no idea who you could become.

text:
That we would do,
We should do when we would; for this ‘would’ changes,
And hath abatements and delays as many
As there are tongues, are hands, are accidents;
And then this ‘should’ is like a spendthrift sigh
That hurts by easing.
plain: Do it when you want to do it. The wanting fades, delays pile up, and sighing about it doesn't help.

text:
One woe doth tread upon another’s heel,
So fast they follow.
plain: Bad things come in a line. Keep your footing.

text: My will, not all the world.
plain: The only thing that can stop you is your own will.

text: To what base uses we may return, Horatio! Why may not imagination trace the noble dust of Alexander till he find it stopping a bung-hole?
plain: Even the greatest conqueror ends up as dirt plugging a barrel. Ambition is humbled by the grave.

text: Imperious Caesar, dead and turn’d to clay, Might stop a hole to keep the wind away. O, that that earth which kept the world in awe Should patch a wall t’expel the winter’s flaw.
plain: The man who ruled the world now fills a crack in a wall. All power ends here.

text: Alas, poor Yorick. I knew him, Horatio, a fellow of infinite jest, of most excellent fancy.
plain: The funniest, liveliest person is a skull in the end. So laugh while you can.

text: Now get you to my lady’s chamber, and tell her, let her paint an inch thick, to this favour she must come.
plain: No amount of makeup stops the skull showing. Don't spend your life on appearances.

text: Is this the fine of his fines, and the recovery of his recoveries, to have his fine pate full of fine dirt?
plain: All that scheming over land, and the payoff is a head full of dirt.

text:
But age with his stealing steps
Hath claw’d me in his clutch,
And hath shipp’d me into the land,
As if I had never been such.
plain: Age sneaks up without a sound and then it's over, as if you were never there.

text:
Let Hercules himself do what he may,
The cat will mew, and dog will have his day.
plain: Even the strongest can't stop the world from running its course. Everyone gets their day.

text:
Our indiscretion sometime serves us well,
When our deep plots do pall; and that should teach us
There’s a divinity that shapes our ends,
Rough-hew them how we will.
plain: Sometimes the plan fails and the reckless move works. Something bigger shapes the result, however you carve it.

text:
It will be short. The interim is mine;
And a man’s life’s no more than to say ‘One’.
plain: The time between now and the end is yours to use. And a life is as quick as counting one.

text: Not a whit, we defy augury. There’s a special providence in the fall of a sparrow. If it be now, ’tis not to come; if it be not to come, it will be now; if it be not now, yet it will come. The readiness is all.
plain: You can't dodge what's coming or predict it. Be ready, and that's enough.

text:
O good Horatio, what a wounded name,
Things standing thus unknown, shall live behind me.
plain: What people believe about you will outlive you, so make sure someone knows the truth.

text: The rest is silence.
plain: In the end there's nothing more to say. Say what matters now.

text:
Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince,
And flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.
plain: A good friend's farewell. Say it the way you'd want it said to you.

text:
Why, as a woodcock to my own springe, Osric.
I am justly kill’d with mine own treachery.
plain: He walked into his own trap. Schemes against others come back to you.

text:
The edge of war, like an ill-sheathed knife,
No more shall cut his master.
plain: Violence you can't control ends up cutting you.

text:
If all the year were playing holidays,
To sport would be as tedious as to work;
But, when they seldom come, they wish’d-for come,
And nothing pleaseth but rare accidents.
plain: Rest feels good because work is the rule. Endless fun turns boring.

text:
And, like bright metal on a sullen ground,
My reformation, glitt’ring o’er my fault,
Shall show more goodly and attract more eyes
Than that which hath no foil to set it off.
plain: A comeback shines brightest against a bad past. Your low point makes the rise look better.

text:
I’ll so offend, to make offence a skill,
Redeeming time, when men think least I will.
plain: Let them underestimate you, then turn it around when they least expect it.

text: Thou didst well, for wisdom cries out in the streets and no man regards it.
plain: Good advice is everywhere and almost nobody listens.

text: ’Tis dangerous to take a cold, to sleep, to drink; but I tell you, my lord fool, out of this nettle, danger, we pluck this flower, safety.
plain: Everything has risk. Grab the nettle and you get the flower.

text:
If we fall in, good night, or sink or swim!
Send danger from the east unto the west,
So honour cross it from the north to south,
And let them grapple. O, the blood more stirs
To rouse a lion than to start a hare!
plain: Go for the big danger. A lion wakes your blood. A hare doesn't.

text:
By Heaven, methinks it were an easy leap
To pluck bright honour from the pale-faced moon,
Or dive into the bottom of the deep,
Where fathom-line could never touch the ground,
And pluck up drowned honour by the locks,
So he that doth redeem her thence might wear
Without corrival all her dignities.
plain: When your sights are set high enough, even impossible leaps feel easy. Ambition at full blast.

text:
Why, so can I, or so can any man,
But will they come when you do call for them?
plain: Anyone can claim big powers. The proof is whether it works when called.

text:
And I can teach thee, coz, to shame the devil
By telling truth; tell truth, and shame the devil.
plain: Telling the truth beats the devil at his own game.

text:
By being seldom seen, I could not stir
But like a comet I was wonder’d at,
That men would tell their children, “This is he.”
plain: Don't be everywhere. Rare appearances make people take notice.

text:
Our hands are full of business. Let’s away,
Advantage feeds him fat while men delay.
plain: Delay feeds your opponent. Move now.

text: Banish plump Jack, and banish all the world.
plain: Cut out the one who brings the joy and you've cut out the world.

text: Sweets to the sweet. Farewell.
plain: A tender goodbye, flowers for the dead.
